blindSummary:
This state/province operates outside the country's federal legal framework in practice. In February 2017, its law-enforcement and security officials launched an anti-gay purge, rounding up dozens of men, holding them in unofficial detention facilities (documented by name and location, including a secret prison in a secondary town), humiliating, starving and torturing them, forcibly disappearing some, and returning others to families “barely alive from beatings” after captors exposed them and encouraged relatives to carry out honour killings (documented by an international human-rights organisation, 2017). An independent national newspaper reported in January 2019 that persecution had resumed and the same town's facility was “full again,” while the head of this state/province's press office publicly denied that any unofficial detention sites exist.

The pattern has mutated and continues: an independent monitoring group documented at least seven cases of this state/province's security forces blackmailing detained homosexual men into “volunteering” for front-line conscription in a war the country fights abroad (one already killed), and a second rights organisation found a mass wave of unlawful detentions tied to forced conscription. In 2021, an aide to the head of this state/province announced the abduction of two men evacuated abroad, seized at a police station in their home town. A foreign home ministry's country-of-origin guidance (June 2025) explicitly names this state/province's wider border zone as the exception to its finding of no state-persecution risk elsewhere in the country.

For a visitor discovered or outed, the evidence indicates near-certain detention without legal process, torture, coerced conscription or death, with no functioning judicial remedy — a very large negative deviation from the country-wide average, reflecting a governance system where the security apparatus operates outside all legal constraint. This sits far below every other unit in the country: even two neighbouring states/provinces that share the same security logic of the wider border zone lack this state/province's documented scale of extrajudicial killing and secret-prison infrastructure.
